question.problem:
The probability mass function of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $-1$ $0$ $1$
$f(x)$ $\frac{1}{3}$ $\frac{1}{3}$ $\frac{1}{3}$

$y$ $1$ $2$
$f(y)$ $\frac{1}{5}$ $\frac{4}{5}$

Find $\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X-\sqrt{5}Y].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y].
$$

Also, the variance of $X$ is determined by the formula 

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

First, let's find $\text{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{X}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =(-1)(\frac{1}{3})+0(\frac{1}{3})+1(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x) \\  & =(-1)^{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{3})+{0}^{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{3})+{1}^{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}-{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{Y}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{5})+2(\frac{4}{5}) \\  & =\frac{9}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}{y}^{2}\cdot f(y) \\  & ={1}^{2}\cdot (\frac{1}{5})+{2}^{2}\cdot (\frac{4}{5}) \\  & =\frac{17}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{17}{5}-{(\frac{9}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\sqrt{3}X-\sqrt{5}Y] & =(\sqrt{3})^{2}\text{Var}[X]+(-\sqrt{5})^{2}\text{Var}[Y] \\  & =3\cdot \frac{2}{3}+5\cdot \frac{4}{25} \\  & =\frac{14}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
